title: Addition, subtraction, double-angle, and half-angle formulas
terms: addition formula; subtraction formula; double-angle formula; half-angle formula; angle sum; angle difference.

exposition.text:
The addition formulas are sin(a + b) = sin a cos b + cos a sin b, cos(a + b) = cos a cos b − sin a sin b,
and tan(a + b) = (tan a + tan b)/(1 − tan a tan b) where all terms are defined. Replacing b by −b

Half-angle formulas are sin(a/2) = ± (1 − cos a)/2 and cos(a/2) = ± (1 + cos a)/2, with signs
determined by the half-angle quadrant. Also tan(a/2) = sin a/(1 + cos a) where defined. Angle
formulas are especially useful for exact values, eliminating inverse trig functions, and reducing
multiple-angle equations to algebra.

question.text:
How many x ∈ [0, 2π) satisfy sin(2x) = cos x?
(A) 2 (B) 3 (C) 4 (D) 5 (E) 6

solution.text:
Double-angle reduction gives cos x(2 sin x − 1) = 0. The first factor contributes π/2, 3π/2; the
second contributes π/6, 5π/6. Dividing by cos x would lose two of these four solutions.
Product-to-sum gives half of cos(π/2) + cos(−π/3), which is (0 + 1/2)/2 = 1/4.

question.text:
Let α, β ∈ (0, π/2) satisfy α + β = π/4. What is (1 + tan α)(1 + tan β)?
√ √
(A) 1 (B) 2 (C) 2 (D) 1 + 2 (E) It depends on α.

solution.text:
Writing u = tan α and v = tan β, the addition formula gives (u + v)/(1 − uv) = 1, hence
u + v = 1 − uv. Therefore (1 + u)(1 + v) = 1 + u + v + uv = 2.
